what.text: Magnesium is a mineral. Under US law, a product with a mineral that is meant to supplement the diet can be sold as a dietary supplement.

what.text: Researchers study it for sleep because it blocks NMDA receptors and supports GABA signaling, two brain systems involved in sleep. That is the reasoning given in trial papers, not a result.

src.label: Abbasi et al., J Res Med Sci, 2012

what.text: Supplements come in many salts, such as magnesium bisglycinate and magnesium L-threonate, which have each been tested in sleep trials. Magnesium sulfate is also an FDA-approved injectable drug, but for other uses.

src.label: Schuster et al., Nat Sci Sleep, 2025
Hausenblas et al., Sleep Med X, 2024
Magnesium Sulfate Injection, USP (Fresenius Kabi) label, DailyMed

what.text: No magnesium product is approved for sleep. Using it for sleep is a supplement use, not an approved one.

research.text: Sleep trials of magnesium are small and short, and they used different salts, doses and measures. A 2026 systematic review of 12 trials rated the evidence low to very low certainty and said it does not support magnesium as a routine insomnia treatment.

research.title: Magnesium for sleep in adults, 2026

facts.v: systematic review of randomized controlled trials of magnesium alone, searched to June 2026
12 trials on sleep, insomnia or poor sleep in adults (plus 3 on cramp or leg-movement sleep problems)
varied
sleep questionnaires, EEG, actigraphy, wearables, body markers

research.found: Findings were inconsistent across measures. Certainty was low to very low. The authors found modest benefit on some self-rated outcomes in some adults and said the evidence does not support routine use for insomnia.

src.label: Lopresti et al., J Diet Suppl, 2026 (systematic review)

research.title: Magnesium for insomnia in older adults, 2021

facts.v: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials vs. placebo
3 trials, 151 older adults, 3 countries
varied
time to fall asleep, total sleep time, side effects

research.found: People fell asleep 17 minutes sooner with magnesium than with placebo. Total sleep time rose 16 minutes, which was not statistically significant. All trials had moderate to high risk of bias, and evidence quality was low to very low.

src.label: Mah and Pitre, BMC Complement Med Ther, 2021 (meta-analysis)

research.title: Older adults with insomnia, 2012

facts.v: double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled
46 older adults with primary insomnia
8 weeks
Insomnia Severity Index, sleep log, blood melatonin, renin and cortisol

research.found: Insomnia scores, sleep efficiency and time to fall asleep improved vs. placebo. Total sleep time did not differ significantly between groups.

src.label: Abbasi et al., J Res Med Sci, 2012

research.title: Magnesium bisglycinate in adults with poor sleep, 2025

facts.v: double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled
155 adults aged 18 to 65 reporting poor sleep
4 weeks for the main result
Insomnia Severity Index and other questionnaires

research.found: Insomnia scores fell by 3.9 points vs. 2.3 on placebo (p=0.049), a small effect. Other questionnaires did not differ. Sleep was not measured objectively. One author runs a research firm funded by supplement companies.

src.label: Schuster et al., Nat Sci Sleep, 2025

research.title: Magnesium L-threonate in adults with sleep problems, 2024

facts.v: double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel groups
80 adults aged 35 to 55 with self-reported sleep problems
21 days
sleep questionnaires; a consumer sleep ring; mood and energy

research.found: Several ring-based scores (deep sleep and REM scores) and some daytime ratings were better than with placebo. The paper declares possible competing interests. Consumer ring scores are not a clinical sleep test.

src.label: Hausenblas et al., Sleep Med X, 2024

us.text: Magnesium can be sold in the US as a dietary supplement. FDA does not approve supplements before they are sold. FDA-approved magnesium drugs, such as magnesium sulfate injection, are for other uses, not sleep. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: minerals are dietary ingredients under the law that defines dietary supplements.

src.label: 21 U.S.C. 321(ff), definition of dietary supplement, govinfo

items.text: under the 1994 supplement law (DSHEA), FDA does not have the authority to approve dietary supplements before they are marketed, and firms generally do not have to give FDA their safety evidence.

items.text: Magnesium Sulfate Injection, USP (NDA 019316) is approved for magnesium deficiency, for magnesium in IV nutrition, and to prevent and control seizures in pre-eclampsia and eclampsia. It is given by a clinician, not for sleep.

side.text: FDA does not review magnesium supplements for safety before sale. The sleep trials were short and reported few problems. Injected magnesium can be dangerous in overdose.

items.text: the 2024 trial reported magnesium L-threonate was well tolerated over 21 days. The 2021 meta-analysis looked at side effects, but its abstract gives no rates.

items.text: adverse effects are usually from magnesium toxicity: flushing, sweating, low blood pressure, weak reflexes, paralysis, low body temperature, and heart and breathing depression leading to respiratory paralysis.
